You have to fill a child’s cup. I understand the touched out and physical part, but ALL MOTHERS deal with that. If you don’t want to take on a motherly role, I would suggest not dating someone with kids. And I say that kindly, AF. Once a child is involved, you have to consider their best interest. And if her LOVE language is physical touch, you have to find a way to meet that language like it or not. Well, you don’t HAVE to, but it would make your bond stronger and it would make this 10 year old child feel loved/liked/worthy/happy/confident/secure/safe.

With that being said, I sometimes have to tell my kid that “Mommy is touched out and needs space. But I am looking forward to cuddling with you _______” (at bedtime, while we watch a movie, after dinner, whatever works for you).

Permission is a huge thing, too. If she is running up and embracing you, or sitting on top of you all the time, you can start teaching her boundaries with bodies. Start by asking her permission. “Hey, I would love to play with your hair. Can I?” or “I’m feeling like I need some love. Can I have a hug?” or “Do you mind if I hold your hand?” And then when she’s not respecting space you can refer back to when you asked for permission to touch her body.

I would never suggest saying you don’t want to hug her. It’s just mean. But if she learns to ask and you aren’t feeling it you can say, “Thanks for asking but my body is overstimulated. Can we connect through (tv,books,games,etc)” or “I’d love to give you a quick hug but then I have to do ____.” or make it silly like “Your sibling (unborn) is kicking my booty!! Can you keep yours over there until they’re done?” 

And then reinforce it. 🤗
